My Kenmore Elite Model 110.66962500 dryer was only getting warm and not hot enough to dry clothes in a reasonable amount of time. This thermostatic switch is used turn the dryer heating element on and off and thereby regulating the air temperature in the dryer.

I removed the original thermostat from the dryer (make sure you unplug the dryer before doing any repair or replacement work on your dryer —- Safety First). I replaced it with this item and now my dryer is working like it should.

Have a older Kenmore dryer that was no longer creating heat. The issue was a fuse that failed, but it was recommended that other sensors also be replaced, otherwise another might fail due to similar age and cause the machine to stop heating again. I replaced that fuse along with this thermostat and a couple others. This stat arrived quickly and was a direct replacement for the original. For a few dollars, it will hopefully keep the dryer running for awhile and keep me from having to pull the machine apart to repair again.

There is a 'flat' on the shaft of the fan, which needs to mate with the flat on the blower fan basket. I don't know if I missed this point in the past, but the motor and blower basket mated perfectly this time. Now the fan runs VERY quiet. For low money, suggest you replace both the motor and the fan basket together so you get that 'flat' on the shaft to mate.

While this motor is easy to install, it's noisier than the 15 year-old motor I replaced. By contrast, I have purchased genuine Nutone OEM motors over the years & the fan was significantly quieter after motor replacement. Motors with a sleeve bearing (instead of a ball bearing assembly) at each end of the rotor & a rotor that may not be perfectly balanced contribute to a louder noise level in operation. Exhaust fans made in recent years have improved designs & reduced noise levels. If you're bothered by the constant, low-pitch rumbling of a noisy replacement motor, it's probably time to replace the whole fan unit - even if it does involve more work. Your ears will appreciate it.

The original Nuton fan motor although oiled occasionally became somewhat noisy after more than 20 years of reliable service. That is why I ordered this replacement motor believing that a new one would surely be quieter. It is a physically perfect replacement for the original motor and installing it is quite simple. If after a few days, this does not improve, I  plan to contact Amazon to return this unit.

This review is just on the installation for my situation as I put the motor in today and have no experience with it long term. The motor went in easily in the old bath exhaust fixture in our upstairs bathroom. The fixture is maybe 80s I believe. When finished and I turned the fan/ light on, the fan did not turn but made a hum. Found out the shaft on this replacement fan protruded out about 1/4" longer than the original and was jammed against the top of the fixture when the mounting screws were tightened. I just removed the fan motor, dented the inside top of the fixture a bit where the shaft was rubbing and reinstalled and it works fine. Quieter than the old original fan motor that finally died. Not a problem really.
